problem: Navigation agents are evaluated mostly on task success, so it is unclear whether they understand language. They ground language poorly (goal-only supervision, no fine-grained attributes or spatial relations), generalize poorly to unseen scenes, and use maps too weak for rich instructions.
motivation: Instruction following needs agents that ground fine-grained language (attributes, spatial relations, route cues) and transfer to new environments and real robots. The thesis observes that what an agent can understand depends on how it represents the world, so it studies representation choices (supervision, 2D category maps, factor-graph topological priors, multi-layer feature maps) across four projects.
key_idea: Match the spatial semantic representation to the linguistic and task complexity: language-aligned supervision (LAW), modular 2D semantic maps (MOPA), LLM-inferred factor graphs (LIFGIF), and multi-layer CLIP-feature maps with a relation graph (MLFM), plus a diagnostic benchmark (LangNav) for language understanding.
insight: Representation should follow the task. A 2D category map suffices for object goals, a topological factor graph suits route instructions, and a multi-layer feature map with a relation graph is needed for attribute and spatial descriptions. Modular designs and decoupling high-level reasoning from low-level control give zero-shot generalization, including to a real robot. In MLFM ablations, more layers help up to 3 (SR 39.5 vs 29.7 with 1 layer), the two-phase EAE-E navigation helps (VLFM-v2 and OneMap-v2 beat their originals), and a VLM reasons better on egocentric images than on top-down projected features.
method: LAW (Ch.3): supervises a CMA agent in VLN-CE with language-aligned waypoints from the reference path (pano or step) instead of the goal-oriented shortest path, improving instruction following (nDTW, waypoint accuracy).

MOPA (Ch.4): modular pipeline of object detection, top-down semantic map building, exploration (uniform sampling works best), planning, and a pretrained PointNav navigation policy. It is zero-shot across scenes and tasks (MultiON 2.0, ObjectNav).

LIFGIF (Ch.5): GPT-4 offline turns an instruction into a factor graph of waypoints and landmarks with Gaussian relations. A factor-graph SLAM (GTSAM) refines it online, CLIP matches landmarks to detections (RAM+GroundingDINO+SAM), and the agent picks waypoints by distance plus uncertainty and navigates with PointNav.

LangNav/LaMoN (Ch.6): a language-guided multi-object navigation dataset on HSSD with GT-attribute, manually verified descriptions, linguistic tags (attributes, spatial relations), and multiple valid goals per description.
MLFM map (Ch.6): a multi-layer top-down map M in R^{L×h×w×fd} storing SED CLIP patch features projected by depth into height layers (3 layers, 6 cm cells).
MLFM querying (Ch.6): vanilla cosine similarity, +VLM (GPT-4 over layer images), or +RGraph, a relation graph with geometric spatial relations and CLIP text-feature triplet scoring.
EAE-E two-phase navigation (Ch.6): explore-and-exploit for the first 40% of steps, requiring map and YOLO-World detector agreement, then exploit-only using the map, with VLFM frontier exploration.

setting.backbone: Mixed across chapters. LAW: CMA (trained). MOPA: pretrained detector + PointNav (trained, modular). LIFGIF: GPT-4 (frozen) + RAM/GroundingDINO/SAM + PointNav + SLAM. MLFM: SED-CLIP + YOLO-World + optional GPT-4 (frozen), zero-shot.
setting.training_data: LAW: R2R VLN-CE trained with waypoint supervision. MOPA/LIFGIF/MLFM: none (zero-shot; only pretrained components, PointNav trained on MP3D/HM3D).
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D with GPS/compass (MLFM, LIFGIF, MOPA); panoramic RGB-D for LAW
setting.action_space: Low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 25 cm, TURN 30° left/right, STOP/FOUND
setting.privileged: none for main methods (oracle detector/navigator only in ablations)

numbers.method: LIFGIF with Oracle detector + Oracle navigator
numbers.backbone: GPT-4 graph inference with oracle detector and navigator
SED CLIP patch features + YOLO-World + GPT-4

numbers.eval_set_note: language goals only; split name not stated in thesis text

numbers_note: Only Ch.5 and Ch.6 tables were present. The LAW (Ch.3) and MOPA (Ch.4) result tables were omitted from the extracted text, so no numbers are given for them. The OC-VLN and LangNav test rows use benchmarks that do not appear in the canonical list. The GOAT-Bench split is inferred, not printed.
results: On the LangNav test split MLFM+RGraph reaches SR 39.5 / SPL 14.9, beating the 2D-map baselines OneMap-v2 (26.7/10.1) and VLFM-v2 (24.8/9.7) and roughly matching EgoImageMap+VLM in SR (35.1/10.9). LIFGIF on OC-VLN gets SR 0.58 / nDTW 0.48, above Seq-VLFM (0.33/0.33) and InstructNav (0.24/0.33). On GOAT-Bench language goals, MLFM+RGraph gets 24.2 SR / 21.5 SPL, versus 21.5/16.2 for Modular GOAT.
limitations: LangNav has no coreference, negation, multi-object relations or action directives, and relations rely on bounding boxes and fixed proximity thresholds.
LIFGIF fails with multiple instances of the same landmark and with detector misclassification; its data association and stopping policy are simple.
MLFM is weak on texture and state attributes, depends on the feature extractor and detector, and fails to separate inside/above/below when objects share a map layer.
